A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same NeCGS work. All 17 pages in each version, including the six-page supplementary material, were readable through text extraction and rendering, supporting comparison of text, equations, tables and figures.

before.justification: v3 reports original compression experiments on four geometry datasets, timing measurements, ablations and qualitative reconstructions in Section 4 and the supplementary material.

after.justification: v4 retains these original compression experiments, timing measurements, ablations and qualitative reconstructions, including the supplementary results.

M1.justification: The TSDF-Def representation, deformable marching cubes, quantization-aware auto-decoder, losses, Huffman coding and decompression procedures are unchanged. Fitting embedded features for newly added shapes also remains identical.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate AMA, DT4D, Thingi10K and Mixed, covering human, animal and CAD geometry. The scenario adding new shapes to a compressed set is also retained unchanged.

E2.justification: Figures 4, 5 and 15 retain GPCC, VPCC, PCGCv2, Draco and QuantDeepSDF as comparators. Table 1 retains the same timing-comparison methods, and the supplementary QuantDeepSDF adaptation is unchanged.

E3.justification: Dataset sample counts, scaling to [-1,1]^3, training budgets and model configurations are unchanged. Both retain CD, NC and F-score evaluation, including the same thresholds and 100,000-point sampling procedure in supplementary Section 3.1.

E4.justification: Section 4.3 retains the same representation and L1-regularization comparisons, auto-encoder versus auto-decoder comparison, SSIM ablation, resolution study and dynamic-scenario demonstration. Their corresponding tables and figures contain the same analyses.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests for the experiments. No statistical reporting practice is added or revised.

E6.justification: Tables 1–3, the rate-distortion curves and the main and supplementary reconstruction results match. For example, Table 1 retains NeCGS compression time of 10.01 hours and decompression time of 98.95 milliseconds; no result entries or findings change.

T1.justification: The TSDF-Def definition, Algorithm 1 and Equations 1–11 are unchanged, including the supplementary quantization, reconstruction-error and metric definitions. No formal assumptions, derivations or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions: a compact geometry representation, neural geometry-set compression and a benchmark. Claims concerning compression approaching 900 times, detail preservation and handling newly added shapes are unchanged.

C2.justification: Both retain the same explanations for poorer compression on more diverse datasets, the emphasis on offline compression and fast decompression, and the resolution-versus-inference-time tradeoff. No substantive limitations or qualifications are added.

D1.justification: Section 4.1 and the supplement retain the same optimization settings, architecture details, hardware, quantization instructions and evaluation implementation details. The source-code access statement and repository address are unchanged.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion and cited works in both the main and supplementary reference lists are unchanged. The positioning relative to point-cloud codecs, implicit representations and prior compression methods is retained.

P1.justification: The first-page arXiv margin label changes from v3 dated 22 May 2025 to v4 dated 26 June 2025. The title, author information, prose and section organization otherwise remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The duplicate arXiv margin stamp on the supplementary material's opening page, PDF page 12, is removed. All 19 figures and three tables retain their content, captions, organization and placement.

improvement.justification: The scientific argument, experimental evidence, mathematical content and reproducibility details are unchanged throughout the main paper and supplement. Updating the version/date marking and removing the duplicate supplementary stamp are cosmetic changes with no meaningful effect on overall paper quality.
